neighbours.label: the '=' that opens a continuation line in a multi-line worked calculation (vs the same calculation written inline in prose)
quiet: Using Newton's second law with 12 kg and 3 m/s^2 gives a force of 36 N.
The cost is the price times the quantity, so 45 dollars for 20 units comes to 900 dollars.
With a radius of 5 cm the area of the circle is about 78.5 square centimeters.
Driving at 60 km/h for 2.5 hours covers 150 km in total.
Revenue was 8,000 and costs were 5,500, leaving a profit of 2,500 dollars.
A 12 volt source across a 6 ohm resistor dissipates 24 watts.
Seven games totaling 420 points give an average of 60 points.
A 4 kg mass moving at 3 m/s has 18 joules of kinetic energy.

notes: Probe: line-initial '=' continuing a derivation 0.905 and 0.605; inline '=' in prose 0.212-0.289; 'we have' line 0.107; prose about equations 0.020. Near misses state the same numbers inline with no '=' sign.
